Emperador rejoins FTSE global equity index after 2-year absence. Emperador Inc., tycoon Andrew Tan’s global liquor conglomerate, is rejoining the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (GEIS) as a Small Cap constituent next month after a two-year absence following its removal in March 2024. The firm’s re-entry comes after FTSE’s Asia-Pacific excluding Japan excluding China Regional Index Semi-Annual Review was announced on Aug. 21, 2026. Revisions to the index can still be made until Sept. 4, with the final list to become effective on Sept. 7, 2026. Emperador is the only Philippine company newly added to the FTSE Small Cap segment in this review. The inclusion places the company within the relevant FTSE Small Cap and All Cap benchmark universes. “The company remains focused on broadening its institutional investor base, improving market liquidity and strengthening its investable market capitalization over time,” Emperador said in a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Monday, Aug. 24. Valued at around $3.8 billion in terms of market capitalization, Emperador is a global brown spirits company with leading brandy and Scotch whisky businesses spanning the Philippines, the United Kingdom (UK), Spain, Mexico and other international markets. It is dual-listed on the PSE and the Singapore Exchange (SGX). Emperador is seeing signs of recovery in its domestic and overseas businesses, particularly in the lower-priced brandy segment. During the firm’s annual stockholders’ meeting (ASM) last June, Emperador President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Glenn Manlapaz said there is a resurgence in the brandy business, particularly in the Philippines, where the company’s products offer more value and match the taste of the younger generation of consumers. “There are also developments in the international markets that is encouraging at the moment and we expect our international brandy business to contribute more to the company in the succeeding years,” he added. Meanwhile, the global whisky business saw a downturn in the past three years because of the high cost of living brought about by geopolitical conflicts, inflation, supply chain disruptions, and the escalating price of petroleum. “We gained volume in our affordable and standard brands globally but that could not make up for the loss, admittedly, in the rare niche,” said Manlapaz. He noted, though, that Emperador’s whisky business was positive in the first quarter of 2026 “because of better sales of premium products and we are starting to see some green shoots.” “If premium is improving, then the market is recovering. And, if that happens, in a while, the rarer niche market, the vintage market, will be back as well. Our brands have retained their strong brand equities despite the downtrading,” Manlapaz explained. Emperador’s whisky brands Dalmore, Tamnavulin, and Jura are still among the top single malts in the world, with Jura at number one in the UK, followed by Tamnavulin, while Dalmore is still the leading luxury single malt in a lot of Asian markets such as greater China, Indochina, and even in Southeast Asia. Thus, he said, “when global economies recover, our brands will definitely still be preferred.” - James A. Loyola

Deutsche Bank sees BSP rate hike to 5% as necessary to tame inflation, protect incomes. Further increasing the key borrowing cost to five percent is needed to curb still-elevated price pressures that are hurting consumers’ pockets, Frankfurt-based Deutsche Bank AG said. Deutsche Bank Research joined the hawkish consensus, pricing in a quarter-point hike at the monetary authorities’ fourth policy meeting for 2026 on Thursday, Aug. 27, and citing the broader impact of inflation. “We see another 25-basis-point (bp) policy rate hike to five percent from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) on Aug. 27 as necessary to further dampen the impact of price pressures on consumers and stabilize real incomes,” Deutsche Bank said in a commentary published last week. Recall that the peso’s purchasing power fell to its weakest level on record in April at 0.73, largely driven by price pressures stemming from the United States (US)-Iran tensions. Filipinos’ buying power has yet to fully recover, as it only picked up to 0.74 from May through July—still hovering near record lows. Based on Deutsche Bank’s assessment, four-fifths of the Philippine consumer basket by weight “are seeing above-trend inflation.” The lender noted that the index persisted despite headline inflation moderating to a three-month low of 6.2 percent in July from the peak of 7.2 percent in April. “This suggests that inflationary pressure in the Philippines is still broad-based and that spillover effects are likely still working their way through the economy, in our view,” Deutsche Bank said. Meanwhile, think tank Capital Economics believes the BSP will shift to a dovish mode after raising the benchmark rate one last time on Thursday, citing the worst output growth—excluding the Covid-19 pandemic—since late 2009. “BSP officials will have one eye on the weakness of the economy,” said Jason Tuvey, deputy chief emerging markets (EMs) economist at Capital Economics. “Alongside the hit to consumer spending due to the energy shock, the economy is struggling with the effects of President Marcos’ anti-corruption campaign.” After the expected last quarter-point hike, Tuvey stressed that monetary authorities will revert to easing once oil prices normalize. Singapore-based DBS Bank Ltd., meanwhile, leaned toward tightening, suggesting there remains no “convincing” trend that would reinforce a pause. “Officials would likely prefer to see a more convincing disinflationary trend before drawing a pause,” DBS chief economist Taimur Baig and senior economist Radhika Rao said. DBS pointed to the balancing act required to address the above-target inflation prints and below-target gross domestic product (GDP) growth figures. It added that the peso’s drift to record lows, alongside the resurgence of oil price hikes, strengthens the call for a “pre-emptive tightening response.” “Beyond a likely hike in August, our baseline forecast is for one more hike within the year before slipping into a prolonged pause,” DBS said. “Policymakers will monitor signs of a potential shift in the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) policy bias as well as US yield movements in the near term.” In contrast, Pantheon Macroeconomics said the disappointing second-quarter GDP outturn, coupled with sustained disinflation, “will be just about enough to dissuade the BSP from hiking further next week.” From the dovish camp, Pantheon Macroeconomics expects interest rates to remain steady at the current 4.75 percent level through the end of 2026. Pantheon Macroeconomics chief emerging Asia economist Miguel Chanco and Asia economist Meekita Gupta lowered their full-year 2026 growth forecast for the Philippines to 2.8 percent—falling short of the already-lowered government growth target of 3.5 to 4.5 percent. “We have reduced our 2026 growth forecast to 2.8 percent from four percent, and 2027 to four percent from five percent, as the recovery looks set to be even more lackluster than we previously thought,” Chanco and Gupta said. Even their 2027 projection falls short of the revised target. “Any investment bounce in the second half is likely to be minor, with industry and construction still operating at below-average capacity and, unsurprisingly, surveyed expansion plans remaining depressed amid plummeting business confidence and flat-at-best market sentiment,” they further said, adding that the slump in public construction has yet to show signs of reaching its lowest point.

‘Saudel’ to briefly enter PAR; direct impact unlikely as it stays offshore — PAGASA. The typhoon with the international name “Saudel” is expected to briefly enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) on Monday afternoon, Aug. 24, but will remain far from the country’s landmass, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said. As of 10 a.m., the center of Saudel was estimated at 1,480 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, outside PAR. PAGASA said the typhoon will be given the local name “Obet” once it enters PAR. Saudel maintained maximum sustained winds of 175 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gustiness of up to 215 kph. It was moving west-northwestward at 30 kph. The typhoon is currently near super typhoon strength and may intensify further into a super typhoon, with maximum sustained winds of at least 180 kph, before entering or while inside PAR. However, PAGASA said Saudel is less likely to directly affect the country’s weather and sea conditions over the next three days. Based on the forecast track, Saudel is expected to exit PAR Monday evening or early Tuesday, Aug. 25. However, a more westward track beyond the next 24 hours could result in Saudel remaining within PAR beyond Tuesday. While Saudel is expected to stay offshore, it is enhancing the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” together with Tropical Depression Gaenari, formerly known as “Neneng.” PAGASA weather specialist Aldczar Aurelio said the habagat is currently affecting Northern and Central Luzon and its effects over Luzon may continue for the next four days. As of Monday, occasional monsoon rains are expected to persist in Batanes. Metro Manila, Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Central Luzon, the rest of Cagayan Valley, Cavite, Batangas, and Rizal will have cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms. The rest of the country will experience partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms. PAGASA is also monitoring two other tropical cyclones outside PAR. Tropical Storm Atsani was located 1,535 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon. It was moving north-northeastward at 10 kph and has a low chance of entering PAR as it interacts with Saudel. Tropical Depression Gaenari was located 505 kilometers north-northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, and was moving southwestward away from the country.

Declogging keeps Baclaran stalls open despite rains. Vendors in Baclaran, Parañaque City kept their stalls open and continued earning despite successive heavy rains that hit Metro Manila over the past two weeks. The absence of flooding in the busy commercial district was attributed to the continuing flood-prevention efforts of the city government under Mayor Edwin Olivarez. Olivarez said the city has been closely monitoring drainage systems and waterways in Baclaran and other flood-prone areas to ensure the continuous flow of rainwater. Through the City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO), daily declogging operations are being conducted while pipe drainage systems are also being installed to improve drainage capacity. The mayor said these measures are particularly important in Baclaran, where thousands of vendors, workers, commuters, and shoppers converge every day. With no floodwater disrupting the area, vendors were able to continue their operations and protect their daily income despite the frequent downpours. Olivarez assured residents and business owners that the city government will continue its drainage maintenance, declogging operations, and other flood-control measures to minimize flooding and protect livelihoods during the rainy season. He also called on the public to help keep drainage systems and waterways free from garbage and other obstructions that could hamper the flow of rainwater.

Grenada establishes diplomatic foothold in PH. The relationship between the Philippines and Grenada may be relatively new, but the Caribbean nation is already putting down roots in Manila. Grenada has formally established an Honorary Consulate in the Philippine capital, giving the country a physical diplomatic presence just over a year after Manila and St. George’s formally established bilateral relations. Business and civic leader Catherine Tiu-Tan will serve as Grenada’s Honorary Consul, following the granting of her exequatur by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. through Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro. The new post, located at The Boni Prime in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig, is expected to handle consular matters while helping develop economic, political, cultural and even sports cooperation between the two countries. For two island nations separated by more than 16,000 kilometers, the similarities may be more significant than geography initially suggests. “Despite the geographic distance between Southeast Asia and the Caribbean, the Philippines and Grenada share identical vulnerabilities, aspirations, and opportunities,” Tiu-Tan said. “The opening of this Honorary Consulate is a definitive step toward bringing our people closer, advancing strategic partnerships, and translating our shared values into actionable solutions.” Tiu-Tan recently met Grenadian Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell during a high-level courtesy call, an early indication of the Grenadian government’s support for the reactivated Manila post. While Grenada previously had an honorary consular presence in the Philippines, the post had long been inactive. Its re-establishment provides Grenadian citizens with a local point of assistance while creating a platform for trade delegations, commercial exchanges and other bilateral initiatives. The timing is also significant. The Philippines and Grenada only formally established diplomatic relations on May 8, 2025, when then Foreign Affairs Secretary Enrique Manalo and Grenadian Minister for Foreign Affairs, Trade and Export Joseph Andall signed a Joint Communiqué on the sidelines of a meeting of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) in Saint Kitts and Nevis. That agreement carried significance beyond the bilateral relationship: with Grenada, the Philippines completed diplomatic relations with all 14 CARICOM member states. The opening of an Honorary Consulate now moves the relationship from diplomatic formalities toward something more practical. Honorary consulates can play an especially useful role for countries without resident embassies, providing representation on the ground while helping identify opportunities that might otherwise be difficult to pursue from thousands of kilometers away. For Grenada, a small Caribbean state with a population of just over 100,000, Manila can also serve as a point of engagement with one of Asia’s most dynamic regions. For the Philippines, the relationship opens another door to the Caribbean at a time when Manila has been widening its diplomatic reach beyond its traditional partners. There are natural areas where the two countries could find common ground. Both are archipelagic developing states confronting many of the same questions surrounding climate vulnerability, disaster resilience, sustainable tourism, food security and the management of marine resources. The new consulate is also looking toward opportunities in trade, culture and sports. What those opportunities eventually produce will depend on the work that follows. But diplomacy often begins simply by making it easier for two countries to find each other. With an Honorary Consulate now operating in Manila, Grenada has made that distance considerably smaller.

How to apply online for the SSS ₱20,000 emergency loan without visiting a branch. Members of the Social Security System (SSS) affected by Tropical Storm “Maymay” and the enhanced Southwest monsoon (habagat) can now apply for immediate financial relief through the agency’s emergency loan program. According to the state-run pension fund, qualified workers nationwide can access emergency funds directly through its official online platform, eliminating the need to visit branch offices in person. To begin the application process, individual members must log into their accounts on the My.SSS online portal via the agency’s website. Before submitting an application, members must ensure their contact details and Philippine home addresses are fully updated in the system. Applicants must also verify that an active bank account or electronic wallet is registered under the portal's Disbursement Account Enrollment Module to facilitate electronic payout. Under updated guidelines enacted in May 2026, members become eligible for the ₱20,000 borrowing ceiling if they have accumulated at least 18 monthly contributions—down from the previous requirement of 36 payments. Applicants must have at least six posted contributions within the 12 months preceding the application date. Self-employed, voluntary, non-working spouse, and land-based overseas Filipino worker (OFW) members must have six monthly payments posted under their active membership category prior to the month of filing. The credit facility carries a 7% annual interest rate with a total repayment timeline of 30 months. The package incorporates a mandatory six-month payment moratorium upon approval, during which no monthly amortizations or penalty fees accrue. Regular monthly payments automatically begin in the seventh month. Members with clear account histories can simultaneously apply for a standard SSS salary loan alongside the emergency facility through the same digital portal. To maintain eligibility, applicants must be under 65 years old and free of past-due balances on previous calamity, salary, educational, or other short-term and long-term loans. Members with outstanding restructured loans, active fraud cases, or final retirement or total disability claims are disqualified.

2026 World Café of Opportunities is set in Caraga region. BUTUAN CITY – The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) will conduct tomorrow, Aug. 25, the 2026 World Café of Opportunities (WCO) through its Job Linkaging and Networking Services (JoLiNS) in Caraga region at the Robinsons North Atrium, Butuan City. The WCO is TESDA’s flagship employment facilitation and job-linkaging initiative that brings together TVET graduates and alumni, jobseekers, employers, industry partners, government agencies, technical-vocational institutions, and other stakeholders in a one-stop-shop platform for employment, skills development, entrepreneurship, and other support services. TESDA Caraga Regional Director Florencio F. Sunico, Jr. said through JoLiNS, the activity also seeks to strengthen the connection between skills training and actual employment opportunities while addressing skills-job mismatch. This big event on Tuesday, Aug. 25 aims to facilitate employment opportunities, improve job-skills matching, provide access to training and competency assessment, and strengthen partnerships among government, industry, employers, and other stakeholders. Sunico said the 2026 WCO was intended to serve TVET graduates and alumni, jobseekers and unemployed individuals, workers seeking upskilling or reskilling opportunities, employers and industries with available vacancies, aspiring entrepreneurs, self employed individuals, returning Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), and individuals interested in TESDA’s training, assessment, certification, and other services. During the event, participants will have access to various stations and booths offering job opportunities and recruitment, career guidance and employment facilitation, training and scholarship opportunities, competency assessment and certification information, skills demonstrations, government services and referral assistance, and industry and employer engagement. Participants will have access to various stations and booths offering job opportunities and recruitment, career guidance and employment facilitation, training and scholarship opportunities, competency assessment and certification information, skills demonstrations, government services and referral assistance, and industry and employer engagement. The activity will be implemented by the TESDA Caraga Butuan City, Agusan del Norte Cluster, in coordination with the TESDA Caraga Regional Office, TESDA Agusan del Norte Provincial Office, Provincial Training Center of Agusan del Norte, Northern Mindanao School of Fisheries, as well as government agencies, private sector partners, employers, industry associations, and other stakeholders. More than simply a job fair, the World Café of Opportunities serves as a convergence of employment, training, entrepreneurship, and support opportunities, designed to connect skills with meaningful economic opportunities, Director Sunico also said. Through this, TESDA Caraga reinforces its commitment to ensuring that every skill counts, every opportunity is accessible, and every TVET graduate is given a pathway toward productive and sustainable employment or entrepreneurship. Sunico also said the activity is expected to generate employment opportunities, improve job-skills matching, increase referrals for training and skills upgrading, strengthen industry partnerships, and generate Hired-On-the-Spot (HOTS) and near-hire applicants. For TVET graduates, jobseekers, employers, and other interested stakeholders, the 2026 World Café of Opportunities is an opportunity to connect, explore possibilities, and turn skills into meaningful opportunities. The activity forms part of the nationwide celebration of the National Technical-Vocational Day, observed every August 25 pursuant to Republic Act No. 10970, and coincides with the 32nd Founding Anniversary of TESDA.

Tinio slams Castro for 'hijacking' school safety issue. House Deputy Minority leader and ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio assailed Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro for turning the discussion on school safety into an issue against teachers. "Presidential Spokesperson Usec. Claire Castro has blatantly hijacked the discussion," Tinio, a member of the Makabayan bloc, said in a statement Monday, Aug. 24. "Yung napakahalagang talakayan tungkol sa school safety naging paniningil sa mga guro at tamang modo," he noted. (The very important discussion on school safety turned into fault-finding against teachers and proper conduct.) Tinio was alluding to Castro's rather unexpected reaction to the deadly Zamboanga City school shooting last Aug. 18 . In her remarks, the Palace official underscored that teachers must do their part in properly guiding students. "Minsan na po nating nakita mismo ang ibang mga guro ay lumalabag sa ganitong klase ng moralidad. Sila mismo ay nagtuturo sa kanilang mga estudyante kung papano maging walang modo lalung lalo na sa mga nakakatanda or sa mga ibang tao," Castro said. (We have already witnessed some teachers themselves violating this kind of morality. They even teach their students how to be disrespectful, especially toward elders or other people.) To this, Tinio said: "Instead of acknowledging the government's shortcomings in addressing the systemic issues that make schools unsafe, from negligent gun owners to chronic underfunding and lack of mental health services in schools to the overall culture of impunity, the Presidential Spokesperson has sought to change the conversation and make it about the alleged online misconduct of individual teachers." "There are remedies available to those aggrieved by online posts, unlike victims of school shootings," he noted. "Ano ang ginagawa ng Malacañang para hindi na maulit ito? Yun ang ipaliwanag mo," he further told Castro. (What is Malacañang doing to prevent this from happening again? That is what you should explain.) The Zamboanga school shooting took place less than two months after the school shooting in Tacloban City, Leyte. There were five student deaths between the two incidents. A House inquiry on the matter has been sought .

Quezon City leptospirosis cases jump 138%. Quezon City recorded a 138-percent increase in leptospirosis cases from Aug. 5 to 18, pushing the number above the city’s alert threshold amid continued rains brought by the southwest monsoon (Habagat). The Quezon City Epidemiology and Surveillance Division (QCESD) recorded 62 new cases and five deaths during the two-week period, involving patients aged four to 74, with a median age of 31. Of the 62 cases, 44 were male, while those affected included seven construction workers, three students, two bicycle drivers, two security guards, one garbage collector, and one delivery rider. From Jan. 1 to Aug. 18, the city recorded 197 leptospirosis cases and 24 deaths, according to QCESD surveillance monitoring. Barangay Commonwealth recorded the highest number of cases during the two-week period with eight, followed by Payatas and Batasan Hills with four cases each. U.P. Campus, Bagong Silangan, and San Antonio each recorded three cases. The Quezon City Health Department urged residents to avoid unnecessary swimming or wading in floodwaters and to wear appropriate protective footwear and clothing if exposure cannot be avoided. Those exposed to floodwater were advised to immediately wash thoroughly with clean water and soap and monitor themselves for symptoms such as fever, headache, yellowing of the skin or eyes, and muscle pain, particularly in the legs. Residents who develop symptoms after floodwater exposure were urged to immediately seek consultation at the nearest health center or hospital. Quezon City health centers offer free post-exposure prophylaxis using doxycycline, but residents were reminded not to take antibiotics without medical consultation and a prescription.

BCDA taps battery maker StB GigaFactory to drive clean energy at Clark. State-run Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) is teaming up with StB GigaFactory Inc. to explore renewable energy (RE) solutions to support ongoing operations and future developments at New Clark City in Tarlac. In a statement, BCDA said it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with StB GigaFactory on Aug. 7 to assess RE solutions, including energy storage systems and e-mobility services, designed to power future-ready industries. The MOU is a 12-month agreement that aims to promote cleaner energy integration, grid reliability, and sustainable mobility infrastructure to establish a modern RE ecosystem in New Clark City. “Partnering with StB GigaFactory aligns directly with our vision to make New Clark City a model of sustainable, high-tech urban development," said BCDA President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Joshua Bingcang. Under the agreement, BCDA will grant site access, supply key project data, and provide administrative assistance to StB GigaFactory. On the other hand, the company will oversee site surveys, technical feasibility studies, and financial modeling to formulate recommendations for clean energy deployment. Bingcang said integrating these energy storage and clean mobility solutions is crucial to building a resilient infrastructure framework that empowers industries operating in New Clark City. StB GigaFactory, a joint venture between Australian-based StB Capital and China-based Oli Power, was the first locator in Filinvest Innovation Park within New Clark City. The company is the country’s first manufacturing plant for lithium iron phosphate battery cells for residential, industrial, and utility-scale battery energy storage systems. New Clark City is expected to soon host more companies in the advanced manufacturing sector, particularly since it is the site of the proposed artificial intelligence (AI) industrial hub under the Pax Silica initiative. The industrial hub is designed to facilitate investments in the manufacturing of AI-related components, including electronic products and semiconductors. Beyond New Clark City, BCDA said the MOU with StB GigaFactory also aims to explore RE solutions in other developments by the state-run firm. “By combining BCDA’s industrial land development platforms with StB GigaFactory’s localized energy storage technology, the partnership demonstrates how utility-scale renewables, energy storage, and electric mobility can be seamlessly scaled,” the agency said. (Dexter Barro II)

184 wanted persons arrested in Baguio from April to July. BAGUIO CITY -- The Baguio City Poluce Office reported a total of 184 wanted persons were arrested by combined police operatives and intelligence units from April 1 to July 22, 2026, as part of the intensified campaign against wanted individuals. BCPO City Director Police Col. Ruel Tagel reported the significant accomplishment during the third-quarter joint meeting of the City Peace and Order Council (CPOC) and the City Anti-Drug Abuse Council (CADAC), noting that the figure surpassed last year's accomplishment for the same period by 21 arrests. Tagel attributed the increase to intensified operations against wanted persons and the continued efforts of law enforcement units to locate and apprehend individuals with pending warrants, whether within or outside the city. He said that while the number of arrested most wanted persons declined compared to the previous year, the BCPO continues to strengthen intelligence monitoring, target profiling, and coordinated operations to facilitate the apprehension of priority fugitives. Meanwhile, the BCPO sustained its campaign against loose firearms, reporting an increase in operations conducted from 47 to 49, resulting in the recovery, confiscation, or surrender of 49 firearms. Tagel said the increased number of firearms removed from circulation reflects the effectiveness of the city's intensified law enforcement initiatives in reducing the possible use of loose firearms in the commission of crimes. The BCPO continues to strengthen checkpoint operations, intelligence monitoring, and public awareness campaigns to promote responsible firearm ownership and ensure compliance with Republic Act No. 10591 or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Law. Tagel emphasized that the continued implementation of these initiatives forms part of BCPO's commitment to enhancing public safety, maintaining peace and order, and preventing criminal activities in Baguio City.

Obiena finishes seventh in Silesia Diamond League. EJ Obiena stumbled against his elite counterparts and settled for seventh place in the Silesia leg of the 2026 Wanda Diamond League in Poland on Sunday, Aug. 23. The two-time Olympian cleared 5.80 meters to finish behind world No. 1 and Olympic champion Armand Duplantis, who captured the gold medal with an impressive 6.20m clearance. Norway’s Sondre Guttormsen turned heads and bagged the silver via countback over Paris Olympics bronze medalist Emmanouil Karalis of Greece after both athletes registered identical 6.00m marks. “A lil 5.80m here in Poland. Para sa bayan,” Obiena wrote on social media moments after the tournament. The 30-year-old Tondo native needed two attempts to clear the opening height of 5.50m, but managed 5.65m and 5.80m with ease. He tried 5.90m twice before risking his final attempt at 6.00m, but failed. Obiena was coming off a sixth-place performance at the Athletissima Lausanne in Switzerland where he posted 5.81m. Prior to that, he won three consecutive gold medals, including a season-best 5.91m feat at the Golden Sand in Poland. Obiena is gearing up for the 2026 Asian Games where he is expected to defend the crown with upcoming tournaments in Zurich, Switzerland.

Gas meters from the GTA 6 leaks are causing a stir. Much like the real world counterpart, gas is looking like an issue in the upcoming, much awaited game, Grand Theft Auto VI. Cyberleeks, an individual or a group, have been posting leaks of Grand Theft Auto VI, mere days from the full unveiling this week–first on Netflix, then on YouTube six hours later. In one of those leaks, a gas icon, with a circle meter, is shown briefly when one of the game’s protagonists, Jason Duval, enters a car. This suggests players would need to watch out for fuel consumption when cruising around. Going through online discussions about this particular feature, players are divided. There is the side who say this will ruin the fun of just driving around Vice City as players need to remain vigilant how much gas is left in their vehicles. Then there’s the other side who say, this will make the game more interesting. While I haven’t personally seen the leaks, I found this gameplay mechanic to be the more interesting. This is for a number of things. This would force players to better take care of their cars, which seems the complete opposite of how GTA is probably best known for, rampant chaos. But that isn’t always true, there are players who definitely just want to cruise around, listen to the radio, and see the sights, basking in the immersion. On a recent playthrough, when finding gas stations, a part of me secretly wished we could actually fill up the tanks, instead of simply pretending to. I cannot be the only one. The new feature would also be useful for GTA roleplayers who immerse themselves fully in the game, and use moments of filling the tanks to strike dialogue with other players. But more on immersion, the gas consumption brings interesting gameplay changes. Imagine trying to flee, and the car your character steals happens to have little gas or no gas at all. It would also mean players cannot keep driving with the same car while evading law enforcement, which to me, seems to be suggesting police chases will remain intense but less aggressive, if that makes any sense. If you watch real life police chases online, you’d probably know what I mean, where the police will hound the fleeing suspects, but won’t try to bring down the wrath of God on them–at least not right away. In previous GTA games, the police will ram players’ vehicles with no regards of consequences, wreaking as much havoc as the players. GTA VI may suggest otherwise, and while in lower starred wanted levels, the police may simply keep chasing players within the city until they run out of gas. The game will also take place in the state of Leonida, which besides containing Vice City, will have massive marsh regions. Imagine running out of gas here. I hope players will have the option to push cars or be able to call for tow truck services. You might say, in such scenarios, the players can simply hope to encounter a passing car to steal, or send themselves straight to the hospital for a pseudo “fast travel.” But, this is where this gets even more interesting. According to the leaks, players cannot carry an entire fortress on them, meaning weapons are limited. Loads will be similar to Red Dead Redemption 2, where you can only choose a set number of weaponry to carry, while the rest is stored in the horse. If this is so, this would mean that cars, at least primary cars, are more important than ever. In GTA V, primary cars always get repaired and return to their parking spot without consequence. If in GTA VI, your primary car gets destroyed, or if the police wastes players, their cars will be impounded, which is strongly suggesting everything inside may disappear. Carefully watching gas would also mean players would find those jerry cans more useful. Players can keep them stocked. And this also brings in an interesting idea, if a player steals a car while in the midst of refueling, would it leave a trail of spilled gas? This could lead to a number of things, like spontaneous fires and explosions. I don’t know about you, but all of that sounds very interesting to me. For some reason, the extended look of Grand Theft Auto VI will premiere on Netflix on August 27. But that’s global dates, which would make it August 28, Friday for us. After the premiere, six hours later, it will go live on YouTube. Grand Theft Auto VI is launching on consoles this November 19, again that’s global dates. So it would be November 20 for us here.

A woman’s guide to perimenopause. Are you in your 40s? You are now entering a crucial stage in a woman’s reproductive cycle: perimenopause. This is a period of transition from a woman’s reproductive years to menopause—a season of change that usually begins four years before the total cessation of a woman’s menstrual periods but could also begin as early as eight to 10 years before menopause. During this period, the body undergoes significant changes due to hormonal imbalances, thus causing a myriad of emotions that may render a woman anxious or, worse, fearful. A woman may begin to experience mood swings, anxiety, and even depression. There are also sleep disturbances brought about by night sweats and hot flashes, as well as palpitations, unexplained weight gain, especially in the belly area, irregular menses, and very heavy menstrual flow that could last longer than the usual number of days. The interval between menstrual periods can also become as short as 21 days. Headaches and other aches and pains are also commonly experienced. Furthermore, as the production of the hormone estrogen declines, a woman’s risk of developing cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, cancer, insulin resistance, and osteoporosis is higher. Decreased metabolism occurs, which alters a woman’s efficiency in burning calories and fat. These changes favor visceral or abdominal fat deposition. Visceral fat causes low-grade systemic inflammation in the body, which increases damage to the heart and blood vessels, as well as targets other cells and organs in the body. Decreased estrogen production also impacts a woman’s appetite. Estrogen helps suppress cravings. Therefore, a woman may experience food cravings during perimenopause. Left unmanaged, this could lead to weight gain and increased body fat, especially visceral fat. We all know the health implications of having excess weight. In 2023, Hungarian Dietetic Association Secretary General Aliz Erdelyi and colleagues conducted a review on the importance of nutrition during menopause and perimenopause. “Menopause is associated with an increased prevalence of obesity, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular diseases, and osteoporosis. These diseases and unfavorable laboratory values, which are characteristic of this period in women, can be significantly improved by eliminating and reducing dietary risk factors,” their study states. “Changing dietary habits during perimenopause is most effectively achieved through nutrition counseling and intervention. To reduce the risk factors of all these diseases, and in the case of an already existing disease, dietary therapy led by a dietitian should be an integral part of the treatment.” Moreover, Aliz and her colleagues emphasized that lifestyle modification greatly influences the strength, frequency, and tolerability of symptoms brought about by the hormonal changes during perimenopause and menopause. Here are some tips on what to do to manage symptoms of perimenopause: Find joy in soy Soy in the form of edamame, soybeans, tofu, freeze-dried soy, and soymilk contains plant hormones, or phytoestrogens, known as isoflavones. It’s a myth that soy causes breast cancer. On the contrary, soy prevents cancer. It also alleviates symptoms of perimenopause, such as hot flashes and night sweats. Soy provides complete protein that is equal to the protein contained in animal products but without the pro-inflammatory side effects. Therefore, soy will not cause an increase in uric acid levels. In fact, it is meat consumption, excess fat, and sugar intake that not only increase uric acid production but also prevent its proper excretion. Soy has omega-3s, which help with heart and immune health. Eat wholesome plant foods Consuming unhealthy fats and refined sugars from processed and ultra-processed foods worsens symptoms of perimenopause and menopause. They contribute to weight and fat gain, as well as increase the risk of developing chronic diseases. Eating vegetables at every meal and having fruits for a snack or dessert will help quell inflammation in the body that is related to symptoms and disease conditions. Aim to eat at least one and a half to three cups of cooked vegetables (double the amount for raw leafy vegetables) and about two to three servings of fresh fruits daily. You can also consume fruits and vegetables in the form of smoothies without added sugars. For convenience, some may opt to consume freeze-dried fruits and vegetables if the availability of fresh produce is a challenge. Move regularly and lift weights Exercising and being physically active throughout the day is not an option. It must be scheduled and formed into a habit. Exercise is medicine. It helps build muscle mass to prevent slow metabolism, thus helping burn more fat. Being physically active aids in the production of the mood-stabilizing hormone serotonin, which is also a precursor for the sleep hormone melatonin. Aim to have at least two and a half hours of moderate-intensity exercise per week and twice a week of strength training. You can also incorporate 10 to 15 minutes of walking two to three times a day. Stand up as much as you can. Pace even when talking on the phone. You can lift stuff, but be mindful of observing proper posture. Practice mindful breathing and other relaxation techniques Anxiety, palpitations, and other symptoms worsen when we forget to breathe properly. Before anxiety hits you, mindfully practice deep breathing upon waking up, before going to bed, in between work, and anytime when you feel tired or when negative emotions start to creep in. A full inhale and full exhale done a few times will definitely help manage your symptoms. Other relaxation techniques include prayer and meditation, guided imagery, coloring and painting, basking in nature, taking walks, listening to classical music and worship songs, yoga, tai chi, singing, and more. Practice sleep hygiene Have a bedtime routine at least an hour before your sleeping time. Take a warm bath, wear comfortable sleepwear, ensure a cool room temperature, avoid gadgets, and avoid fighting sleepiness. Wear a sleep mask or earplugs if light and noise prevent you from getting good-quality sleep. Lastly, pray and meditate as you do deep breathing right before snoozing. Perimenopause can be a better life journey for a woman who is willing and able to adopt positive lifestyle changes. Choose to be positively better during perimenopause. cheshireque@gmail.com

Marcos checks relief efforts for flood evacuees in Pampanga. President Marcos has visited an evacuation center in Bacolor, Pampanga, to check on flood-affected families and oversee the government's continuing relief efforts as thousands remain displaced across the province. Marcos visited the Bacolor Integrated School Evacuation Center in Barangay Cabambangan on Monday, Aug. 24, where he spoke with evacuees and observed the distribution of P10,000 cash assistance to heads of affected families under the Department of Social Welfare and Development's (DSWD) Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) program. As of Aug. 23, about 216 families, or 836 individuals, had been staying at the evacuation center for 16 consecutive days. Before the President's arrival, the DSWD had distributed family food packs and served hot meals through its Mobile Kitchen. There were 11 active evacuation centers in Bacolor serving 559 families, or 2,221 individuals, according to authorities. Marcos was accompanied by Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) Secretary Rex Gatchalian, Pampanga Vice Governor Dennis Pineda, Bacolor Mayor Eduardo Datu, and other national and local government officials. In Pampanga, the DSWD reported that 315,807 families, or about 1.01 million individuals, were affected by the enhanced Southwest Monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, with 3,118 families, or 11,308 individuals, still staying in evacuation centers. Flooding was reported in several cities and municipalities across the province, while 10 roads, government facilities, and flood-control structures were damaged, along with four totally damaged houses and 47 partially damaged houses. Agricultural losses and damage were estimated at P423.84 million, affecting 8,742 farmers and fisherfolk, prompting authorities to declare a state of calamity throughout Pampanga on Aug. 12. The DSWD has provided P243.37 million worth of assistance to affected families and made available P2.63 million in standby funds and 127,947 family food packs at its Regional Field Office III. Additional family food packs are available at DSWD Disaster Resource Centers and other field offices for deployment to affected families in Central Luzon as needed. Meanwhile, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has also proposed several long-term interventions to address perennial flooding in the province, including dredging works; Phase 2 of the Pampanga Delta Development Project; construction of the Central Luzon Pampanga River Floodway and Rio Chico Control Structure; construction of the Manila Bay Coastal Defense Dike Project, which will span Metro Manila, Bulacan, Pampanga, and Bataan; and construction of revetments, culverts, detention basins, and dams.

Hontiveros backs stricter gun control. ILOILO CITY—With two deadly school shootings in less than two months, Senator Risa Hontiveros is backing calls for stricter gun control. “I really favor stricter firearms regulation,” Hontiveros told the media while in Iloilo City last August 21. The lady senator said she supports calls to review and make necessary amendments to Republic Act No. 10591 or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act after a student shot and killed a fellow student and would eventually kill himself in Zamboanga City last August 18. Hontiveros reiterated that there was particularly a need to look into existing regulations, especially for law enforcement officers with government-issued firearms. Both fatal school shootings in Tacloban City and Zamboanga City involved firearms issued to law enforcement officers—a police officer and a Bureau of Customs (BOC) security commander. “They are supposed to have the knowledge and responsibility in securing their firearms,” Hontiveros pointed out. Hontiveros said gun-related violence and gun-related incidents could be reduced if the proliferation of firearms is lessened. On the other hand, prevention of school shootings should have a multi-faceted approach. Hontiveros said there is no one-quick solution and there are many factors involved that need the cooperation of the whole community. Meanwhile, Hontiveros assured the other matters would still be discussed as she chairs the Senate Committee on Women, Children, Family Relations and Gender Equality.

Marcos admin to boost middle-class support, protect 6.5M lifted from poverty — Recto. The Marcos administration will step up efforts to protect 6.5 million Filipinos who have moved out of poverty while pursuing measures to create jobs, raise incomes, and reduce living costs for the middle class, Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said. “That is the marching order of the President: Support the middle class and prevent 6.5 million Filipinos from sliding back into the zone of poverty,” he said. Recto cited the sharp decline in poverty incidence from 15.5 percent in 2023 to 9.7 percent in 2025, which reduced the number of poor Filipinos from 17.5 million to 11 million, three years ahead of the administration's target of bringing poverty incidence down to single digits by 2028. However, the Palace official said this was not the time for the government to rest, saying the goal is not the finish line. “Ang susunod nating hamon ay siguraduhing tuloy-tuloy ang pag-angat nila (Our next challenge is to ensure that their progress continues),” Recto said. “Hindi na muling babalik sa kahirapan ang mga nakaahon na, at dadami ang makakaahon pa. At mas protektahan pa natin ang ating middle class (Those who have risen out of poverty must not fall back into it, more people must be lifted out of poverty, and we must further protect our middle class),” he added. Recto said the government could not afford to become complacent as the continuing crisis in the Middle East posed risks to fuel and food prices, trade, employment, and economic growth, while climate disruptions could also affect economic activity. He said the government was addressing these risks through a program to fast-track high-impact infrastructure projects to generate jobs, stimulate local economies, reduce logistics costs, and attract investment. The administration is also pursuing measures aimed at lowering household expenses and increasing disposable income, including a proposal to raise the personal income tax exemption to P350,000 annually, which Recto said could free up to P17,500 a year for each worker. Other legislative measures being pushed by Malacañang include exempting small businesses from the Minimum Corporate Income Tax, granting a general tax amnesty, and abolishing the travel tax. The administration is also seeking amendments to the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) to prevent distribution utilities and electric cooperatives from passing system loss charges on to ordinary consumers, as well as the proposed Sariling Kuryente Act to simplify and reduce the cost of installing household solar and battery systems. Recto said the government would continue prioritizing price stability measures to keep food, fuel, electricity, and other basic necessities affordable while providing targeted assistance to sectors vulnerable to economic shocks. He cited the Expanded UPLIFT assistance for 7.5 million families and the Bawat Bayan Makikinabang Rice Program for 8 million households as examples of government efforts to shield vulnerable Filipinos from economic shocks. The administration will also seek to capitalize on the country's competitive advantages in artificial intelligence and the digital economy, with public investments expected to support better schools, improved health care, and modern infrastructure. Recto said these executive and legislative measures form part of a broader strategy to reduce poverty while building a larger and more resilient Filipino middle class.

Eala rises to No. 18, becomes Southeast Asia’s highest-ranked female player. Alex Eala carved out another historic milestone in her flourishing career, rising to a career-high No. 18 in the latest Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) rankings. The 20-year-old Filipina star jumped two notches from No. 20 ahead of the US Open scheduled this week where she is slated to compete in the singles and the mixed doubles with Canadian Felix Auger Aliassime. Eala’s latest ranking made her the highest ranked female player from Southeast Asia in history, surpassing the previous feat of Indonesia’s Yayuk Basuki and Thailand’s Tamarine Tanasugarn, who both ranked as high as No. 19. Basuki reached her career-best ranking in October 1997. During that year, she finished in the quarterfinals of the Wimbledon and the second round of the US Open. She retired in 2013. Tanusagarn, for her part, matched Basuki’s feat in May 2002. A quarterfinalist of the 2008 French Open, she had four singles and eight doubles career titles before retiring in 2020. Eala’s latest feat is expected to boost her campaign in the final Grand Slam of the season, where she hopes to surpass her best Grand Slam showing -- a fourth-round finish at Wimbledon a few months ago. She will first plunge into action in the mixed doubles, teaming up with Auger-Aliassime against married tennis couple Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina in the opening round.

OCD warns ‘Saudel’ may worsen ‘habagat’ impacts as 7.5 million individuals already affected. The country is bracing for another round of prolonged rains as a new tropical cyclone could further aggravate conditions in areas still reeling from weeks of monsoon rains that have already left 29 people dead and affected 7.5 million others. Office of Civil Defense (OCD) Deputy Administrator for Operations, Assistant Secretary Bernardo Rafaelito Alejandro IV, said the agency is closely monitoring the possible interaction between (international name) Typhoon “Saudel” and the southwest monsoon (habagat), which could bring more rain to western and northern Luzon, including the National Capital Region (NCR). As of Monday, Aug. 24, the latest OCD data showed that the combined effects of enhanced habagat and Tropical Cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng have already affected 2.2 million families or about 7.5 million people in 10 regions. “The overall situation that could affect us is that the habagat is expected to remain active. It could be enhanced or intensified because there is a storm approaching,” Alejandro said. As of writing, Saudel was still outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) and Alejandro said it could be given the local name “Obet” once it enters PAR. He said the enhanced monsoon could begin affecting the country as early as Monday or Tuesday, Aug. 25, and bring prolonged and rapidly intensifying rainfall to areas that have already received heavy rains in recent weeks. “If you remember, it rained continuously last week because of the monsoon. These are the same areas that could be hit by the habagat,” he said. Alejandro said those areas are already saturated, raising the risk of renewed flooding and landslides. He also warned of possible disruptions to critical lifelines, including transportation. Meanwhile, President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. led a meeting at the Pampanga Provincial Capitol on the effects of the habagat and previous cyclones and the preparations of government agencies for areas that could be hit by enhanced monsoon rains. OCD Administrator Undersecretary Harold N. Cabreros and Deputy Administrator for Operations Assistant Secretary Laurena Mina attended the presidential meeting with other members of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC). Likely scenarios According to Alejandro, the OCD is considering two possible scenarios as Saudel approaches. Under the first scenario, the cyclone would enhance the southwest monsoon and produce light to moderate or moderate to heavy rainfall from Monday through Thursday or Friday. “The likely impact would be prolonged rainfall, flooding, and landslides. River levels could rise and water could possibly be released from dams,” Alejandro said. Such conditions could disrupt transportation services and further hurt agriculture because of excessive rainfall and waterlogging, he added. The second scenario involves a change in Saudel’s projected track that could bring the cyclone farther south and closer to Taiwan instead of its earlier projected path toward Japan. “If the track goes farther south, beyond the NCR, there could be an interaction between the habagat and the storm. Again, this could enhance the rainfall that may be brought over western and northern Luzon,” Alejandro said. He said the second scenario would also raise the possibility of strong winds and rough seas while worsening the risks of flooding, landslides, and other hazards. Preparations for Saudel The OCD conducted a Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA) on Sunday, Aug. 23, with government agencies, local governments, and science agencies, including the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) and the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB). The assessment covered the expected weather conditions, possible hazards, and preparations needed in areas likely to be affected. Alejandro said the agency was coordinating with its regional offices, national government agencies, and local governments to ensure that response teams, equipment, food and non-food items are ready for deployment. The OCD said its central and regional offices were also continuing response operations for the effects of previous cyclones and habagat while preparing for the possible combined effects of Saudel and habagat. Water replenishment However, Alejandro said the incoming rains could also have a positive effect by replenishing dams and reservoirs, although authorities would have to closely manage any excess water. “The rainfall will bring water that could raise the levels of our dams or reservoirs. This is an opportunity for us to have water resource recovery, but of course, we will monitor this because it might also lead to the down streaming of excess water. That is why we need to closely watch our flood management,” he said. Over 33,000 individuals still in evacuation centers; 102 areas under a state of calamity The prolonged rains have since affected 418 evacuation centers where 9,858 families or 33,358 people were still staying. Some 2,500 houses were damaged, including 285 that were totally destroyed. Infrastructure losses have reached P5.1 billion while agricultural damage stood at P1.7 billion. Meanwhile, government assistance provided to affected communities has reached P1.31 billion. The government has also declared 102 cities and municipalities under a state of calamity, including areas in Pangasinan, Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro. The OCD urged residents in low-lying and landslide-prone areas to remain alert and follow government advisories. People in coastal communities and those planning to travel were also advised to avoid sailing or making trips when weather conditions deteriorate.

Accident-prone Marilaque Road in Quezon claims life of yet another biker. INFANTA, Quezon- A 22-year-old young man was killed after the motorcycle he was driving collided with a van on Sunday afternoon, along Marilaque Road, Barangay Magsaysay, here, Aug. 23. The victim was identified as Oca, of Brgy. Sampaloc, Tanay, Rizal. At about 2:30 p.m., the victim was travelling along the accident-prone road from Tanay, Rizal, heading to the town proper while the suspect, Erwin, 44, was driving a van with registered plate no. NAC 5107, was travelling in the opposite direction towards Manila. Upon reaching a sharp curve, the vehicles collided near the broken center line of the road. As a result of the impact, the Hi-Ace van's left-side window glass was shattered. The victim sustained serious injury when hisneck was struck by the broken window glass, causing him to fall onto the road. Oca was taken to Claro M. Recto Hospital, where he was pronounced dead by the attending physician. Pili Ani turns local ingredients, touch, food, and hospitality into a wellness experience. Filipino wellness may not yet be as well known internationally, but many of the things associated with it are already part of everyday Filipino life. We care for one another through touch, food, hospitality, and the simple act of making someone feel looked after. Pili Ani co-founder Mary Jane Ong believes the way Filipinos care for one another can also define what makes wellness distinctly Filipino. This led to the opening of the Pili Ani Lifestyle Spa at Greenhills Mall in San Juan City, where the homegrown beauty brand combines local ingredients, touch, and Filipino hospitality through its philosophy, Philippine Wellness Rituals. Founded in 2016 by mother-and-daughter team Rosalina Tan and Mary Jane, Pili Ani built its skincare and body-care lines around two ingredients from the same Philippine pili tree: pili oil and elemi oil. “We want Filipinos to confidently claim our place in the global care and wellness space,” she tells Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. “Care is one of our country’s greatest strengths, and Philippine Wellness Rituals transform that strength into a distinctive beauty and wellness tradition we can proudly share with the world.” Two oils from one tree Pili oil is extracted from the pulp of the fruit and contains naturally occurring carotenoids, fatty acids, and antioxidant compounds. Elemi oil comes from the resin of the same tree and is used in both fragrance and skincare. Pili Ani tests its formulations through Repeat Insult Patch Testing or RIPT, dermatological assessments, comedogenicity testing, consumer-perception studies, and matched photography to document changes over time, working with testing partners abroad as part of its ongoing research. “The benefits I am most confident about are the moisturizing and nourishing properties of pili oil, together with its naturally occurring carotenoids and antioxidant compounds. For elemi, we are especially encouraged by its skin-conditioning properties and its potential to support firmer-looking skin.” It started with a farmer Pili Ani’s beginnings trace back to Bicol and a pili farmer named Noli, who remains one of the company’s suppliers today. Traditionally, the nut was the part of the pili fruit that could be sold. Pili Ani began using the pulp for oil, giving farmers another way to earn. “For us, success is not only about creating beautiful products. It is also about finding more ways for Filipino ingredients to create jobs.” Where to start at the spa Mary Jane recommends two treatments to first-time guests. The Hair Ritual focuses on the scalp and hair and uses Pili Ani’s Restore & Protect Hair Mask. Her other recommendation, and the treatment she feels best represents Philippine Wellness Rituals, is Face Fitness. “Just as we exercise and tone the muscles of the body, Face Fitness uses intentional movements and massage techniques to stimulate and work the facial muscles while creating a deeply relaxing experience.” A taste of local There’s also Café 1197, a free-standing café that guests can visit even without booking a spa service. Its menu highlights Filipino ingredients and the communities behind them. Mary Jane’s daughter, Kiara, and her best friend, Trixie, created Café 1197 together. The name 1197 comes from their shared birth month and year, November 1997. Signature drinks include the Iced Pili Salted Cream Latte, made with Mt. Apo coffee, pili, and sea-salt cream; the Iced Salted Caramel Tibuok, inspired by Filipino artisanal salt-making; and the non-coffee Iced Ube Latte. The menu also includes an Iced Guava Sparkler. Mary Jane hopes that, in time, Filipino wellness will also become more familiar to people outside the country. “We want Filipino wellness to be remembered for its intentional care: thoughtfully produced local ingredients combined with genuine warmth, skilled touch, and heartfelt hospitality.”

Thai prime minister meets security chiefs after coordinated attacks in 3 southern provinces. BANGKOK (AP) — Thailand ’s Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, already facing a flood crisis in the country’s north, held an urgent meeting on Sunday with high-level security officials in response to coordinated violence overnight in three southern provinces where a small-scale Muslim insurgency is active. The meeting, held shortly before Anutin flew north to inspect the badly flooded province of Nan, followed 51 incidents on Saturday night in the southernmost provinces of Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala. The attackers did not engage with military or police forces. Only three civilians were known to have been wounded, and they were reported to be recovering on Sunday. The violence primarily involved small bombs, arson and other forms of property damage. The highest-profile target was a 7-Eleven convenience store in Pattani. A video circulating on social media appeared to show armed men stalking outside the store while customers and workers fled before it was set on fire. A bomb that damaged rail tracks in Narathiwat forced the suspension of local and long-haul services. It was not clear when they would be restored due to the uncertain security situation. As has often been the case with such incidents, no group was immediately publicly blamed or claimed responsibility for the actions. However, such attacks are generally believed to be carried out by the Barisan Revolusi Nasional Melayu Patani, or BRN. It is the major insurgent group in the south with the organizational means and support to stage such an action. It is also the group with which the Thai government has been holding on-again, off-again peace talks. The three southernmost provinces are the only ones with Muslim majorities in predominantly Buddhist Thailand and the BRN has said that it is seeking self-rule for them. Muslim residents have long complained of being treated like second-class citizens in Thailand, and separatist movements have been periodically active for decades. Insurgent violence escalated sharply in 2004 and was met with heavy-handed crackdowns, further fueling discontent. According to Deep South Watch, a think tank based at the Prince of Songkla University’s campus in Pattani, 7,837 people have died in the violence in the past 22 years. The last major flare-up came in July, when about 10 attackers opened fire and threw pipe bombs at soldiers at a security checkpoint in Narathiwat. Five paramilitary soldiers were killed and six civilians were wounded, including a 10-year-old boy. Don Pathan, an independent security analyst, says the BRN carries out attacks largely for leverage as it negotiates with the Thai government. “From the ground, BRN combatants are turned off by the boasting of military officials and wanted to use the spike in violence to demonstrate their capabilities," said Pathan. "Many of the targets in these latest incidents were civilians, but BRN combatants were not after body counts. They want to send a stern message to the Thais of what they are capable of doing.”

BOI grants green lane status to ₱392-billion projects, unlocking 44,000 jobs. The Board of Investments (BOI) granted green lane status to nearly ₱392 billion worth of investments in the seven months through July, enabling them to benefit from expedited processing of permits. Data from the BOI showed that 22 projects worth a combined ₱391.84 billion were certified under the green lane program, which are expected to generate 44,235 jobs. Projects under the renewable energy (RE) sector accounted for the biggest share of the endorsed investments, with 18 projects amounting to ₱386.77 billion in investments. These projects are projected to create 44,016 jobs. The BOI approved two projects in the food security sector, with a combined investment of ₱980 million, which are expected to create 102 jobs. The two remaining projects were endorsed in digital infrastructure and public-private partnership (PPP), infrastructure, and water, with investments amounting to ₱3.43 billion and ₱670 million, respectively. Established under Executive Order (EO) No. 18, the green lane program streamlines the approval process for permits and licenses for strategic investments to accelerate project implementation. Since the program started in February 2023, the BOI has certified 244 projects with a total investment value of ₱6.36 trillion and estimated to create 425,454 jobs. The RE sector continued to be the leading contributor to green lane investments, with 187 endorsed projects amounting to ₱5.46 trillion. The PPP, infrastructure, and water sector generated the second-highest investment value, with ₱416.75 billion for six projects. Meanwhile, the digital infrastructure sector accounted for 10 projects with investments amounting to ₱405.12 billion. Also certified for green lane status were seven manufacturing projects reaching ₱67.04 billion, 33 food security projects worth ₱19.68 billion, and a pharmaceutical project with a project cost of ₱45 million. According to the BOI, 23 projects endorsed under the green lane program, with a total value of ₱286.17 billion, are now operational. The bulk or 166 of the certified projects worth ₱5.52 trillion are in the pre-development stage, driven largely by the RE sector. Meanwhile, 46 projects worth ₱368.64 billion are currently under construction, while nine projects with an aggregate cost of ₱190.21 billion are in the pre-operation stage.

Cordillera to celebrate Special Holiday on 40th ‘Sipat’ anniversary. BAGUIO CITY -- Malacañang has declared September 11, 2026, as a special non-working day in the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) in observance of the 40th anniversary of the signing of the Mount Data Peace Accord. This replaces September 13, the actual anniversary, which falls on Sunday. It can be recalled that Apayao Governor Elias Bulut, Jr., head of the Regional Development Council, requested that September 11 be declared a special day of rest in the region instead of September 13 so that the people can fully participate in the occasion. The request was immediately acted upon by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto who signed Proclamation No. 1389 under the authority of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. This day marks the 40th anniversary of the 1986 "Sipat" or Mount Data Peace Accord, the first peace agreement successfully entered into by the national government with armed groups in the history of the country's peace process. On September 13, 1986, the Government of the Philippines led by President Corazon Aquino and the Cordillera Bodong Administration-Cordillera People’s Liberation Army (CBA-CPLA) led by rebel priest Conrado Balweg entered into a peace agreement at the Mount Data Hotel in Bauko, Mountain Province. This historic event brought an end to hostilities between the rebel armed group and government forces in the region. The agreement paved the way for the inclusion of a provision in the 1987 Constitution for the establishment of an autonomous region in the Cordillera and the signing of Executive Order 220 on July 15, 1987, for the creation of the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) in preparation for becoming an autonomous region. In his recent State of the Nation Address, President Marcos Jr. said that the government is ready to formalize the historic completion of the CBA-CPLA peace agreement.

Tengco blames e-wallet delinking, Middle East crisis as Pagcor earnings take hit. Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (Pagcor) Chairman Alejandro Tengco has pointed to e-wallet delinking and the Middle East oil crisis as reasons for its reduced revenue in 2025. In a budget briefing held Monday, Aug. 24 on the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) by the House Committee on Appropriations, Pagcor noted that its earnings fell by P5.68 billion in 2025, and that it expects to record even lower earnings this year due to weaker gaming operations. "From 2025 to 2026, there were so many events that transpired. Number one was the delinking in September or toward the last quarter of last year of the e-wallets doon po sa mga customers (from the customers)," Tengco told appropriations panel chairperson Nueva Ecija 1st district Rep. Mikaela Angela "Mika" Suansing. Pagcor said gaming activity dropped sharply in late 2025 after e-wallets were delinked from online platforms. "So after that was implemented, we experienced a downtrend of about 40 percent i n gaming activities," Tengco said. Tengco cited a recovery of sorts in the early part of 2026, but "Unfortunately, the Middle East crisis happened." "Truly, both the land-based casinos who were our licensees were affected, and so with online gaming. As you very well know, in the online gaming market, our main customers come from the C,D, E market. And they, that market was the one truly affected by the Middle East crisis," he told the congressmen. From P111.71 billion in 2024, total income of Pagcor fell to P106.03 billion in 2025. Gaming revenue also decreased by P2.38 billion, from P97.52 billion in 2024 to P95.14 billion in 2025. For this year, Tengco noted signs of recovery anew, as gaming activity climbed by 10 percent in July. He said it held steady in August, alongside growing tourist patronage of integrated resorts. Pagcor's debt to PSC Meanwhile, Pagcor bared that it will allocate about P300 million monthly to pay its debt to the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC). This follows the Supreme Court’s final decision setting the computation of Pagcor’s contribution to the PSC. According to Tengco, the agency previously paid only 5 percent of gaming revenue to the PSC based on the old interpretation of the law. But in the final ruling issued in late 2025, the SC mandated that the contribution must be 5 percent of Pagcor’s gross income. Because the ruling is retroactive to 1993, Pagcor owes the PSC about P37 billion. The court granted Pagcor up to 10 years to settle the amount, equal to about P3.7 billion annually or over P300 million monthly. Tengco said this will greatly affect funds that could have been allocated to other nation‑building programs and assistance to various sectors, but Pagcor must comply with the SC’s final decision.

Senate panel OKs bills resetting 2026 BSKE polls, fixing terms of barangay officials. A Senate panel on Monday, Aug. 24, approved bills postponing the November 2026 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) and fixing their term of office. Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero, who presided over the Senate Committee on Local Government hearing, said that his bill, Senate Bill No. 2387, seeks to fix, and not merely extend or postpone, the terms of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials from four to five years, to promote greater stability and continuity in barangay governance. "The natural effect will, of course, be to postpone the upcoming election, but the subject matter of this bill is fixing the term,” he explained. Escudero believed that establishing a fixed five-year term breaks the cycle of repeated congressional postponements and prevents local elections from repeatedly overlapping with national elections. When asked about the postponement, Escudero said it will still be discussed and voted upon in plenary by senators. Under the proposed measure, the transition would count existing terms to ensure fairness, preventing incumbent officials from benefiting from a term extension. The bill also seeks to enable local leaders to focus on long-term community development, disaster response, and peace and order without the disruptions of frequent elections. Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Erwin Garcia said that Congress shall be the sole authority to fix the term. "Yung aming patuloy na pakiusap [sa mga mambabatas], itong buwan ng September, kahit ikalawang linggo man lang, maging maliwanag na 'yung sagot sa katanungan kung tuloy o hindi ang BSKE (Our continued appeal to lawmakers is that by September, even by the second week, there should already be a clear answer to the question of whether the BSKE will push through or not)," he said in a change interview. Meanwhile, Senator Imee Marcos filed the measure seeking to move the November 2026 BSKE to October 2027, noting that the election this year will fall exactly on All Souls’ Day. In a Facebook post on her page, Marcos stated: "Yes! Di na tuloy ang BSKE sa November (Yes! BSKE will no longer proceed in November)." Marcos said the passage of the bill into law would help Filipinos bear the cost of traveling, as the high cost of fuel could bar them from the polls and from exercising their right to suffrage The senator said moving the date to October 2027 would help relieve Filipino families from financial strain especially since they would have to go to the provinces during election day. She said a postponement of the BSKE would give voters more time to transfer their registrations, allowing them to update records and avoid expensive travel on election day. Funds spent Senate President Win Gatchalian asked how much of the Comelec’s expenditures would be lost if Congress resets the elections as part of a proposal to extend the terms of barangay and SK officials to five years. Garcia said around ₱3 billion of the ₱8 billion already spent or obligated for the 2026 BSKE would be considered sunk costs if the elections are postponed again. The 2026 BSKE has been allocated ₱19.57 billion, nearly twice the usual ₱11 billion to ₱12 billion cost of a BSKE. Garcia attributed the higher allocation to the increase in registered voters to about 71 million, the expansion of polling precincts to 225,000, additional electoral board members and support staff, higher teacher honoraria, and increased printing requirements. Garcia said about ₱8 billion has already been spent, obligated or earmarked, including expenses for voter registration, personnel services, overtime work and election preparations. Of that amount, around ₱3 billion would no longer be recoverable. However, Garcia stressed that much of the remaining expenditure could still be used in a future election. He said Comelec has already completed the printing of ballots, including the additional ballots needed for the increase in voters, at a cost of about ₱2.4 billion. If the BSKE is moved to 2028, Garcia said Comelec could issue a resolution allowing the ballots printed for the 2026 elections to be used for the postponed polls, even if the date printed on the ballots remains 2026. Sen. Chiz Escudero, meanwhile, noted that expenses for overtime workers involved in printing and storing the ballots should not necessarily be treated as money wasted, since these form part of the cost of producing and storing election materials that can still be used in a future election.
